meta.title: KalangoOS — the Linux where AI agents work with you
meta.description: Technical preview 0.1 of a Linux distribution where AI agents run on your computer, ask before anything risky, follow rules enforced by the kernel and record what they do, so you can undo what changed.

download.title: Download KalangoOS 0.1 (technical preview) — KalangoOS
download.description: How to download, verify and try the KalangoOS 0.1 technical preview: ISO, binaries, checksums and requirements.
download.lead: The installable ISO and the binaries live on the GitHub releases page, with checksums. Read the warnings before installing.

blocks.text: Technical preview 0.x. The system can break, was tested only in virtual machines (UEFI), the real-hardware matrix is not complete and there are no updates with restore yet. Use it in a virtual machine or on a computer with no important data.
Where the files are: version 0.1.0 is published on GitHub, and the ISO, the binaries, SHA256SUMS and the build provenance attestation are attached to the v0.1.0 release.

items.title: kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso
items.text: The ISO: a live session with the installer. x86_64, UEFI (CI tests with UEFI). It carries no AI model.

items.title: SHA256SUMS-iso.txt
items.text: The ISO's SHA-256 checksum. See how to verify it just below.

items.title: kalangoos-0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
items.text: The compiled programs (shell, kalangod, agent, approval, login and installer). Not an installer: it is for people who assemble their own session.

items.title: SHA256SUMS.txt
items.text: The SHA-256 checksum of the binaries archive.

blocks.title: Verify the file before using it

items.title: Download the ISO and SHA256SUMS-iso.txt into the same folder and check the sum
items.text: The ISO's line must end in OK. If it says FAILED, delete the file and download it again; never use an ISO that does not match.

items.title: Check the origin (optional, needs the GitHub CLI)
items.text: Each release carries a build provenance attestation, showing the file came out of the repository's CI pipeline. It does not prove the code was reviewed, and the ISO is not signed yet.

blocks.title: Try it in a virtual machine (recommended)

items.title: Use the repository script (the simplest)
items.text: With qemu-system-x86 and ovmf installed and no root. The script creates an empty 40 GB virtual disk (DISCO=, MEM=, CPUS= and RES= adjust it), boots the ISO with UEFI firmware and opens the live session with the installer; the live account kalango has no password. After installing, imagem/rodar-iso.sh with no argument boots the installed disk first.
items.code:
git clone https://github.com/kalangoos/kalangoos && cd kalangoos
KALANGO_ISO=/path/kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso imagem/rodar-iso.sh novo

items.title: Or, without the script: create a 40 GB virtual disk
items.text: CI installs and boots the system like this, with QEMU and UEFI firmware (the ovmf package). Other UEFI VM programs may work, but they have not been tested.
items.code:
qemu-img create -f qcow2 kalango.qcow2 40G
cp /usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_VARS_4M.fd uefi-vars.fd

items.title: Boot the ISO with 8 GB of memory and 6 CPUs
items.text: The empty disk falls through to the ISO; after installing, the disk boots the system. Without /dev/kvm the VM is slow.
items.code:
qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu host -machine q35 -m 8192 -smp 6 \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE_4M.fd \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=uefi-vars.fd \
  -drive file=kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso,media=cdrom,readonly=on,if=none,id=cd -device ide-cd,drive=cd,bootindex=1 \
  -drive file=kalango.qcow2,format=qcow2,if=none,id=disco -device virtio-blk-pci,drive=disco,bootindex=0 \
  -device virtio-vga-gl,xres=1920,yres=1080 -display sdl,gl=on \
  -device virtio-keyboard-pci -device virtio-tablet-pci -nic user,model=virtio-net-pci

blocks.title: Install on a computer (at your own risk)

items.title: Write the ISO to a USB stick
items.text: Replace /dev/sdX with the USB stick. Check with lsblk: picking the wrong disk erases your data.
items.code:
lsblk
sudo dd if=kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync

items.title: Boot from the USB stick in UEFI mode
items.text: The live session opens the installer (the live account has no password). The installation writes to the disk you choose: back up first.

blocks.title: AI models come afterwards
paras: The published ISO carries no AI model, because the model's licence is still under review. The installer has an AI models step, and you can change it later in Settings and the App Center. You choose the source: the public one, a private server, a folder or a USB stick. Downloads resume where they stopped and are checked by SHA-256.
Without a model installed the interface works, but the agents do not answer. The default is LFM3 1.7B, about 1 GB.

items.title: Minimum (planned)
items.text: 64-bit processor with 4 cores (x86-64-v2), 8 GB of memory, a 64 GB SSD, Intel, AMD or NVIDIA graphics with Vulkan, and UEFI.

items.title: Recommended
items.text: 8 cores, 16 GB of memory, a 256 GB NVMe and a dedicated graphics card. For larger local models, 32 GB.

items.title: What was tested
items.text: Virtual machines (QEMU/KVM in the automated tests). Real hardware (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) and Secure Boot were not tested yet; Kalango Remote was not tested between two physical computers.

security.title: Security and privacy — KalangoOS
security.description: How KalangoOS limits what agents do, what it does not guarantee, this site's privacy and how to report a security flaw.
security.h1: Real power, with limits you can check
security.lead: Agents operate the system through a single service, kalangod. This page says what stands today, what does not yet and how to reach us about a flaw.

items.title: System approval
items.text: Risky actions ask for approval on a screen drawn by the compositor, out of the agent's reach; forging it is treated as a security flaw. With no answer, the request is denied.

items.title: Four power levels
items.text: Observe, user, system and total. The total level needs in-person approval each session, for 15 minutes, with everything recorded.

items.title: Rules in the kernel
items.text: Landlock, seccomp, cgroups and eBPF LSM, with no kernel module of our own. Protected folders stay locked even for the total level.

items.title: What is read is data
items.text: Pages, files and tool answers do not become commands. On the way out to the web, a rule blocks a local secret pasted, split into parts or encoded (base64, hex, percent-encoding) in the address.

items.title: Timeline and Undo
items.text: Each action is recorded from kernel events and can be undone; before changing the system there is a restore point.

items.title: Allowed folders
items.text: Agents' commands and file tools only write to allowed folders; files that run at login and PATH folders ask for approval; KalangoOS's own configuration is out of agents' reach.

items.title: d1 recommendation in approvals (optional)
items.text: The approval screen shows the recommendation of d1, a small local model that helps, and the decision is the person's; the “Aprovar sozinho o que é de baixo risco” option in Permissions is off by default and only covers moving to trash, moving and creating a new file that does not run, only if the d1 says it looks safe with at least the minimum confidence, never after content read from outside, up to 5 per request, switching itself off after 3 denials, with kalangod checking again and installing packages never counting as “safe”.

items.title: Kalango Remote: privacy mode
items.text: When someone controls with access nobody approved here (a fixed password or unattended access, which has no files, terminal, camera, tunnel, restart or privacy mode), the local screen is covered (“tela preta aqui”) while the controller sees the real desktop. Emergency exits: Esc Esc, switching virtual terminal, the power button and the lock. There is also two-step verification, a global lockout after attempts and a notice to the person being recorded.

blocks.title: What KalangoOS does not guarantee
items: No external security review has been done; it is planned before 1.0.
It is a 0.x preview: there are flaws we do not know yet. Do not use it with data you cannot lose.

The rule blocks a local secret pasted, split into parts or encoded (base64, hex, percent-encoding) in the address; it does not cover rot13, reversed text, a secret split across parameters or the body of a POST.
The local model can be wrong or be tricked. Kernel rules and approval exist precisely because it cannot be trusted alone.
Whoever approves decides. An approval given without reading counts as permission.
The ISO and the binaries are not signed: they only have the build provenance attestation and the SHA-256 checksum.
Using Kalango Remote opens access to another person or machine: do it only with people you know and approve each request.
d1 is a small local model that helps the person decide; it can be wrong. That is why automatic approval is off by default and limited to a few reversible actions.

Kalango Remote: privacy mode, two-step verification and recording were not tested between two physical computers nor in a real (non-nested) niri session; Mosh was not tested; the lock-screen path under the cover is only covered by code, not by a test.
Secure Boot and TPM were not tested, and neither was real hardware (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel).

items.title: Models on this computer
items.text: LFM3, LFM3-VL and LFM3-Audio run through llama.cpp on a local socket, with no network port. There is no cloud AI provider today.

items.title: What can leave
items.text: Searches and pages an agent reads on the web; the model download from the source you chose; and Kalango Remote connections, which you start (a Cloudflare tunnel, end-to-end encrypted). The Privacy now panel shows what left today.

items.title: You see who uses what
items.text: Microphone, camera and screen in use show in the bar; Super+Shift+P pauses everything; Wi-Fi networks can be kept out of agents' reach.

items.title: No trackers
items.text: No cookies and no analytics. If you sign in to the members area, the sign-in service (auth.kalangoos.com, Cloudflare) keeps an 8-hour session cookie; once login is on, every page asks that service once, so it sees your IP address. The members area also loads files and avatars from GitHub.

items.title: What stays in your browser
items.text: Only your theme choice (light or dark), in localStorage, on your computer. There is no form; your GitHub account only comes into play if you sign in to the members area.

items.title: Hosting
items.text: The site is served by GitHub Pages, which may log visits as GitHub's policy describes. The project does not receive those logs.

items.title: Use GitHub's private report
items.text: In the repository, Security tab, Report a vulnerability. Do not open an issue, pull request or public discussion about a flaw.

items.title: Tell us what you saw
items.text: The version or commit, the component (kalangod, kalango-agente, shell, installer, niri patches), the steps to reproduce and the impact. Do not test on computers or accounts that are not yours.

items.title: What to expect
items.text: A reply within 5 business days confirming receipt, assessment, a fix and an agreed disclosure date. Credit in the advisory, if you want. There is no security e-mail yet.

contribute.title: Contribute — KalangoOS
contribute.description: How to contribute to KalangoOS: issues, development environment, house rules, pull requests and coding agents.
contribute.lead: The project is new and moves fast. Contributions in Portuguese or English are welcome: before writing code, say in the issue what you plan to do.

blocks.title: From first look to pull request

items.title: Read the README and the roadmap
items.text: To know what exists and what comes next.

items.title: Find an issue or open one
items.text: Check whether someone already works on it (by #N number and keywords). There are templates for a bug, an idea and a screen. Big changes become a proposal in the issue first.

items.title: Set up the environment and run the checks
items.text: Ubuntu 24.04 or newer. CI runs exactly these commands.
items.code:
sudo apt install build-essential clang libbpf-dev pkg-config libgtk-4-dev libvte-2.91-gtk4-dev \
  libpoppler-glib-dev libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev
poc/setup-deps.sh
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked
cargo test --workspace --locked --exclude kalango-agente

items.title: Open a small pull request
items.text: One subject per pull request, with tests that fail without the change, saying what you tested and what you could not run. main only changes through pull requests and CI must be green.

items.title: Design first
items.text: Every new screen or visible change is born in the Design System before the code, and the implementation matches it. No screens from another system (GNOME, Yaru, Adwaita).

items.title: The system's look
items.text: No shadows, subtle corners, colours only from the tokens and screens that adapt to any space.

items.title: Rust, and English in code
items.text: Our programs in Rust; new identifiers in English; interface text in Portuguese through the translation catalogue.

items.title: No personal data
items.text: Names, Wi-Fi networks, e-mails and files in code, tests and captures are always made up.

items.title: Third-party assets
items.text: Images, icons and fonts only with a compatible licence, listed in ATTRIBUTION.md in the same change.

items.title: Done means done
items.text: Say what you tested and what you could not run. Do not describe as done something that still has gaps.

blocks.title: Coding agents
paras: Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) follow AGENTS.md. A person answers for what the agent opens, comments and sends. Agent-engine tests use the real local model, never a fake one.

items.label: Security flaw? Do not open an issue
items.text: Use the private report.

notes.title: 0.1.0 release notes — KalangoOS
notes.description: What went into the KalangoOS 0.1.0 technical preview, what was left out and the known limitations.
notes.lead: The first KalangoOS release: the installable ISO, the binaries and the code of the agents, kalangod and the desktop. These notes follow the repository's docs/NOTAS-0.1.0.md and CHANGELOG.md. It was tested only in virtual machines.

blocks.text: Status: published. The files are attached to the v0.1.0 release on GitHub, with SHA256SUMS and the build provenance attestation.

items.title: Installable ISO
items.text: x86_64, UEFI. The release workflow builds the ISO and tests it in a VM on every run: the live session boots with the installer, the installer engine writes to an empty virtual disk (the graphical “AI models” step is not exercised by the test) and the installed system boots into its session.

items.title: Installer and model source
items.text: An “AI models” step: choose where models come from (public catalogue, private server or a folder), also in Settings and the App Center. Downloads resume and are checked against a SHA-256 sum (#33). d1-Omni-2B joined the catalogue (#40).

items.title: Approval with d1
items.text: The approval screen shows the recommendation of the d1 decision model (“looks safe” or “looks dangerous”, its confidence and a reason from a closed list); the decision stays with the person. In Permissions, the “Aprovar sozinho o que é de baixo risco” option is off by default: it covers only three reversible actions in the person's folder (move to trash, move, create a new file that does not run), only if the d1 says it looks safe with at least the minimum confidence, never after content read from outside in the conversation, at most 5 per request, and it turns itself off after 3 denials. kalangod re-checks everything, and installing packages is never “safe” (#42).

items.title: Kalango Remote
items.text: Screen sharing, remote control, SSH and Mosh (Mosh not yet tested). A fixed password and unattended access with limited permissions (no files, terminal, camera, tunnel, restart, input blocking or privacy mode; the banner lists what was granted), two-step verification (TOTP), session recording (Videos › Kalango Remote, 30 days, with a notice to the recorded person), its own RustDesk-compatible server, a global lockout after wrong attempts and the agent plan panel (kalango-remote agent-plan) (kalango-remote#11 and #12).

items.title: Remote privacy mode (“tela preta aqui”)
items.text: While someone controls with access nobody approved on this computer, the local screen is covered and the controller sees the real desktop. Emergency exits: Esc Esc, a virtual-terminal switch, the power button and the lock (niri patch 0012, kalangoos/niri#4, and #44).

items.title: Flows and Kalango VirtualDesk
items.text: A full flow editor in the shell; the d1 model also answers in “Decidir” blocks. kalangod has the vm.* tools and the shell has the Settings › Sandbox screen (the vm.* tools ask a single question, #40); the VirtualDesk app is not on the ISO.

items.title: Verify the checksum
items.text: In the downloads folder, the ISO's line must end in OK.

items.title: Verify where the build came from
items.text: GitHub Actions build provenance attestation; needs the GitHub CLI.

items.title: Try it in a VM
items.text: In the repository, with qemu-system-x86 and ovmf installed and no root. The script creates an empty 40 GB virtual disk, boots the ISO with UEFI firmware and opens the live session with the installer (the live account kalango has no password).
items.code:
git clone https://github.com/kalangoos/kalangoos && cd kalangoos
KALANGO_ISO=/path/kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso imagem/rodar-iso.sh novo

items.title: Choose the AI models
items.text: The ISO ships no local model. In the installer's “AI models” step (or later, in Settings and the App Center), choose the public catalogue, a private server or a folder with the models.

blocks.title: Also in
items: Its own shell in Rust and GTK 4 on a patched niri: bar, dock, side bars, desktop, lock screen, login screen, windows and spaces, and the system apps (Files, Settings, Terminal, Editor, Calculator, Agent Hub and more).

kalangod: approval on a screen the agent cannot imitate, Undo, a Timeline and four power levels (observe, user, system, total), with kernel-enforced rules (eBPF LSM, Landlock, seccomp and cgroups), a folder allow-list for writes and the system configuration out of agents' reach.

Local agents with LFM3 through llama.cpp, conversation context management (recent window, background summary and search in the conversation) and agents that operate the screen by vision, always with approval.
Agent and Remote: the remoto.conectar tool lets the agent propose a connection to one of the person's computers through the Remote plan panel; only a person's click approves (#44).
Kalango Audio on the image: capture, process, route and record sound.

Defence against local data leaving in a web address: a secret pasted, split or encoded is blocked in the covered cases (#36); the limits (rot13, reversal, base32/58, XOR, interleaved noise, a secret split across parameters or DNS labels, a POST body and the fragment) are in docs/SEGURANCA.md.
url 2.5.9 against RUSTSEC-2026-0592 (#37) and the Help dictation that stops when its window closes (#38).
Shell memory: closed app windows release their graphics surface after 60 s (#35).

blocks.title: What is not in 0.1.0
items: Updates with a restore point and the recovery screen.
Signed images and packages and the external security review.
Hybrid mode with the cloud and the system in English.

blocks.title: Known limitations
items: Real hardware: tested in VMs only (UEFI); the NVIDIA, AMD and Intel matrix is incomplete.
Local model: the models' licences are under review; the ISO ships no model, it is downloaded afterwards.
Accessibility: not certified or audited.
Language: UI and docs in Brazilian Portuguese; English comes in phase 6.

Kalango Remote: not tested between two physical computers nor in a real niri session (nested only); Mosh was not tested (it is not installed where we tested); the lock-screen path and the screen-transition frame under the privacy-mode cover are only covered by code, not by a test.
VirtualDesk and Flows: not on the ISO; the flows service lives in a private repository.
Updates: no update with a restore point and no recovery screen.
Documentation licence: the proposed CC BY-SA 4.0 is still to be confirmed.
Security: no external review; the limits of the web-address defence are in docs/SEGURANCA.md.

login.title: Sign in with your GitHub account
login.text: The KalangoOS task board is restricted to people in the kalangoos GitHub organisation. The technical documentation and the specification are public: they come from the open repository and appear here for convenience only.
login.error: We could not finish signing in (the request expired, was declined or GitHub did not answer). Try again.
login.down: We could not check your session right now (GitHub or the sign-in service did not answer). Your session is kept; try again in a moment.
login.fine: We ask for read access only: your membership of organisations (read:org) and projects (read:project). Nothing is published in your name, and the session lives in a protected cookie of the sign-in service, never in the browser's storage.

download.title: Download KalangoOS 0.1
download.lead: The installable ISO, the binaries and the checksums are on the v0.1.0 release on GitHub, with the build provenance attestation.

edition.label: Technical preview · 0.1.0
edition.title: KalangoOS 0.1.0
edition.text: Live session with the installer. x86_64, UEFI. The AI model is downloaded later.

items.title: Minimum (planned)
items.text: 64-bit, 4 cores (x86-64-v2), 8 GB of memory, 64 GB SSD, Vulkan graphics and UEFI.

items.title: Recommended
items.text: 8 cores, 16 GB, 256 GB NVMe and a dedicated graphics card. For larger models, 32 GB.

items.title: Tested
items.text: Virtual machines (QEMU/KVM). Real hardware and Secure Boot not yet.

steps.title: Try it in a VM
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/kalangoos/kalangoos
cd kalangoos
KALANGO_ISO=…/kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso \
  imagem/rodar-iso.sh novo

steps.title: Write it and boot in UEFI
steps.code:
sudo dd if=kalangoos-0.1.0-amd64.iso \
  of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync

download.warn: Technical preview 0.x: tested only in virtual machines (UEFI). Use it in a VM or on a computer without important data.
